newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan April foreign currency deposits fall.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan April foreign currency deposits fall.

text.p: Taiwan's foreign currency deposits outstanding fell to T$327.6 billion at the end of April from March's T$333.9 billion, a central bank official told reporters on Wednesday.
The bank attributed the drop in part to profit-taking on U.S. dollars by investors as the greenback had appreciated against the Taiwan dollar in April.
Despite the U.S. dollar's recent weakness against the yen, heavy domestic demand for the U.S. currency had driven the Taiwan dollar steadily lower.
On Wednesday, the local unit closed at T$27.801 against Tuesday's T$27.775 close.
Asked about the local unit's downtrend, Tuan Chin-sheng, deputy head of the central bank's foreign exchange department, said the movement in the foreign exchange market reflected normal demand.
"The forex market is very stable," Tuan told a news conference. He did not elaborate.

Foreign currency deposits had remained high recently as exporters gradually grow used to paying their imported raw materials directly in foreign currency to avoid interest rate fluctuation, central bank officials had said.

Communist China's military threat has also triggered surges in foreign currency deposits. China has viewed Taiwan as a renegade province since a civil war spilt them 1949. It vows to retake Taiwan by force if it opts for independence.
At the time of heightened tensions in the Taiwan strait in the run-up to the March 1996 presidential election, many people transferred their money to foreign currency holdings.
The central bank had said the actual capital outflow was not so serious as speculated as most of the money remained in Taiwan.
